key_points: NVIDIA Dynamo's Shadow Engine Recovery reduces LLM inference outage time from 283 seconds to 7.3 seconds by keeping a pre-initialized shadow engine ready on the same GPUs.
The GPU Memory Service (GMS) allows weight sharing between engines, avoiding the need to reload weights from storage during recovery.
Shadow engines precompute non-transferable components like CUDA graphs and communicators, enabling rapid activation during failover.
The system uses a shared lock and GMS to manage memory and coordination, ensuring reliable and fast recovery without cold restarts.
Shadow Engine Recovery is currently in preview and requires specific Kubernetes configurations, with plans to expand support and stabilize the implementation.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo introduces Shadow Engine Recovery, a feature that significantly reduces the time required to recover from LLM engine failures. When an engine process fails, the standard cold restart involves loading weights from storage, compiling kernels, and capturing CUDA graphs, which can take several minutes. Shadow Engine Recovery keeps a pre-initialized shadow engine idle on the same GPUs as the active engine, allowing it to take over almost instantly. The GPU Memory Service (GMS) enables weight sharing between engines without duplicating memory, ensuring the shadow engine can immediately resume serving. Testing showed that recovery time dropped from 283 seconds to 7.3 seconds, minimizing service disruption. The system uses a shared lock and GMS to manage memory and coordination between engines, enabling rapid failover. While the feature is in preview, it aims to improve reliability for large-scale LLM deployments.
items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo's Shadow Engine Recovery Reduces LLM Inference Outage Time

items.summary: Diffusers now integrates Nunchaku Lite, enabling 4-bit quantized diffusion inference without requiring a separate engine. Users can load pre-quantized checkpoints via from_pretrained() and quantize new models using the diffuse-compressor toolkit. The method achieves up to 50% VRAM reduction and 30% latency improvement, though it lacks the full speed of the original Nunchaku engine due to the absence of architecture-specific fused kernels.

items.summary: MIT researchers have developed a system called FloatForm, which uses a swarm of small robotic boats to autonomously assemble and reconfigure floating structures on water. Each robot, about 21 centimeters square, operates with its own thrusters, sensors, and magnetic latches, enabling them to self-organize into bridges, platforms, or other structures with minimal human input. The system draws inspiration from ant rafts, where individual agents follow simple rules to create resilient formations. The robots communicate with their immediate neighbors to navigate, avoid collisions, and adapt to disturbances, allowing for parallel movement and scalability. The project, published in Nature Communications, aims to transform underutilized water surfaces into dynamic, programmable spaces for urban environments, emergency response, and temporary infrastructure. The team tested the system in controlled environments, achieving high success rates with minimal human intervention, and plans to scale it for real-world applications such as canals and harbors.
items.title: MIT Researchers Develop Self-Organizing Floating Robots for Dynamic Water Infrastructure

items.summary: A pre-registered trial in Sierra Leone found that an AI-powered learning tool, Guided Learning, significantly improved math scores and student engagement. key_points: Google Research developed PHRM, a smartphone-based system that passively measures heart rate and resting heart rate using facial video captured by the front-facing camera.
PHRM uses deep learning and temporal shift convolutional neural networks to estimate heart rate with a mean absolute percentage error under 10%, meeting industry standards across all skin tones.
The system integrates daily heart rate data to estimate resting heart rate with an accuracy comparable to wearables, achieving a mean absolute error under 5 beats per minute.
PHRM was validated through both controlled laboratory studies and real-world 'free-living' trials, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse populations and conditions.

The research highlights the potential of smartphones to provide accessible, wearable-like heart health insights, addressing inclusivity and accuracy challenges in remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) measurements.
items.summary: Google Research introduces PHRM, a system that passively measures heart rate and resting heart rate using smartphone cameras during everyday use. The system leverages deep learning and facial video captured after face unlock events to estimate heart rate with a mean absolute percentage error under 10%, meeting industry standards across skin tones. PHRM also estimates daily resting heart rate with an accuracy comparable to wearables, achieving a mean absolute error under 5 beats per minute. The study, published in Nature, includes the largest and most diverse dataset of smartphone videos for research and a pre-trained model for accessibility. The system addresses challenges in detecting photoplethysmography (PPG) signals in darker skin tones, improving inclusivity and accuracy. PHRM's performance was validated through both controlled laboratory settings and real-world 'free-living' studies, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse populations. The research highlights the potential of smartphones to democratize heart health monitoring, offering wearable-like insights through ubiquitous devices.
items.title: Google Research Introduces Smartphone-Based Heart Rate Monitoring System for Passive Health Tracking

items.summary: Google Research has open-sourced its hydrology model to aid flood forecasting globally. key_points: Amazon and vendors use a combination of VCG and CPP to improve supply chain coordination.
The system, called Flo Pro, enables cost-effective collaboration without full disclosure of proprietary cost data.
VCG ensures truthful reporting by calculating transfer payments based on each party's externality.
CPP provides the computational framework for iterative optimization without requiring full utility function disclosure.
The approach supports dynamic, rolling-horizon planning and offers an alternative 'menu-of-contracts' method for lower-dimensional decisions.
items.summary: Amazon and its vendors face challenges in optimizing supply chain operations due to information asymmetry. The article explains how the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) framework, combined with Amazon's consensus planning protocol (CPP), creates a system called Flo Pro that enables cost-effective collaboration. This system allows both parties to achieve socially efficient outcomes without fully revealing proprietary cost structures. The VCG mechanism ensures truthful reporting by calculating transfer payments that reflect each party's externality on the other. CPP provides the computational backbone, enabling iterative optimization without requiring full disclosure of cost data. The approach was tested successfully with a major manufacturer, demonstrating real-world cost savings. The system supports dynamic, rolling-horizon planning and offers an alternative 'menu-of-contracts' method for lower-dimensional decision spaces. The work highlights the potential of mechanism design in supply chain coordination and opens new questions for future research.
items.title: Amazon and vendors use mechanism design to improve supply chain coordination

items.summary: Amazon has embedded responsible AI (RAI) into every phase of its AI model development, from pretraining to post-training and evaluation. The company's approach includes four key phases: pretraining, post-training, evaluation, and third-party monitoring. Senior scientist Chentao Ye explains that pretraining involves teaching models foundational RAI principles using diverse datasets, including internal and public guidance, to ensure adaptability across languages and cultures. Post-training uses reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align models with human expectations and policy guidelines. Evaluations focus on creating model-breaking datasets to test for unsafe responses, while third-party collaborations address systemic risks like AI-enabled CBRN research. Amazon has developed over 70 RAI tools, published 500+ research papers, and provided extensive training to employees, emphasizing a proactive, three-pronged strategy for responsible AI implementation.
items.title: Amazon integrates responsible AI into all stages of model development

Industry adoption of AstaBench is growing, with organizations like the UK AI Security Institute and General Reasoning integrating it into their evaluation frameworks.
The benchmark highlights uneven progress across categories, with significant gains in code execution but limited improvements in end-to-end discovery.
Costs for top-performing models have risen sharply, with Claude configurations being the most expensive despite their strong performance.
items.summary: AstaBench, an open benchmark for evaluating AI agents' scientific research capabilities, has released updated results showing improved performance on coding, reasoning, and data analysis tasks. The benchmark tested models like GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, with the latter achieving the highest score at 58.0%. However, end-to-end discovery remains challenging, with GPT-5.5 scoring 52.9% and struggling with complex workflows. The benchmark also gained industry adoption, with organizations like the UK AI Security Institute and General Reasoning integrating AstaBench into their evaluation frameworks. The results highlight uneven progress across categories and rising costs, emphasizing the need for continued development in full scientific workflows.
items.title: AstaBench benchmarks AI agents' scientific research capabilities with new results and industry adoption

key_points: NIST released a new annotated fingerprint dataset and open-source software for forensic use.
The dataset includes 10,000 fingerprints with detailed quality annotations for training purposes.
OpenLQM software assesses fingerprint quality and is now available for global use.
The tools aim to improve accuracy and efficiency in forensic analysis and AI training.
Experts and examiners have praised the resources for enhancing objectivity and collaboration in the field.
items.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released a new annotated fingerprint dataset and open-source software to aid forensic scientists. The dataset, part of NIST Technical Note 2367, includes 10,000 fingerprints from 200 volunteers, with annotations detailing print quality. These annotations help train both human examiners and AI systems to evaluate fingerprint quality. NIST also released OpenLQM, a modified version of the LQMetric software, which assesses fingerprint quality and is now open-source. The tools aim to improve accuracy and efficiency in forensic analysis. NIST computer scientist Greg Fiumara noted that the resources will enhance education and algorithm training for fingerprint identification.
items.title: NIST Releases Annotated Fingerprint Dataset and Open-Source Software for Forensic Use

key_points: NIST submitted its annual report to Congress on NCST Act activities for FY 2025.
The Champlain Towers South collapse investigation has completed most of its technical work.
NIST also addressed the impacts of Hurricane Maria on Puerto Rico and implemented Joplin tornado recommendations.
The NCST Advisory Committee praised the investigation's thoroughness and its potential to improve building safety practices.
The Champlain Towers South team plans to present its next findings in a video update in June 2026.
items.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has submitted its annual report to Congress detailing progress on the National Construction Safety Team (NCST) Act activities for fiscal year 2025. The report highlights the completion of most technical work on the Champlain Towers South collapse investigation, including material testing, full-scale replica tests, and data analysis. It also covers NIST's work on Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico and actions taken to implement recommendations from the Joplin tornado investigation. The NCST Advisory Committee noted the investigation's thoroughness and expects its methodologies to improve building safety practices. The team plans to present its next findings in June 2026.
items.title: NIST Completes Major Technical Work on Champlain Towers South Collapse Investigation

key_points: Leanstral is an open-source code agent designed for Lean 4, aiming to improve formal verification through code generation and proof.
The model, with 6B active parameters, outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance.
Leanstral was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean.
The project is accessible via Mistral Vibe, a free API, and allows users to run the model locally under an Apache 2.0 license.
items.summary: Leanstral, an open-source code agent for Lean 4, aims to enhance formal verification by generating code and proving its correctness. The project, developed by researchers, introduces a model with 6B active parameters, optimized for proof engineering tasks. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, available through Mistral Vibe and a free API. Leanstral outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance, achieving higher scores with lower computational cost. The model was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean. The team emphasizes its accessibility, offering zero-setup integration and the ability to run the model locally.
items.title: Leanstral: Open-Source Code Agent for Formal Verification

key_points: An autonomous agent was developed to generate and refine RSpec tests for Rails applications, addressing the gap in test coverage.
The agent uses Vibe with custom tools like RuboCop and SimpleCov to ensure test quality and execution, improving test scores from 0.68 to 0.74.
The agent operates in parallel across multiple file types, using specialized skills for each category to avoid code duplication.
LLM-as-a-judge metrics were used to evaluate test quality, though they lack determinism and cannot catch syntax errors.
The experiment showed the agent successfully improved test coverage, achieving 100% for previously uncovered files.
items.summary: An autonomous agent was developed to address the issue of insufficient test coverage in large Rails monoliths. The agent reads source files, generates or improves RSpec tests, validates them against style rules and coverage targets, and runs within a CI/CD pipeline without human intervention. It operates in parallel across multiple files, handling different file types like models, controllers, and helpers with specialized instructions. The agent uses Vibe, a coding assistant, with custom tools like RuboCop and SimpleCov to ensure test quality and execution. By enforcing a strict self-review process and using LLM-as-a-judge metrics, the agent improved test quality scores from 0.68 to 0.74. The experiment showed that the agent successfully generated tests for uncovered files and improved existing ones, achieving 100% coverage. However, challenges like syntax errors and versioning issues highlight the need for ongoing refinement.
items.title: Autonomous agent improves Rails test coverage by generating and refining RSpec tests

key_points: Amodei attributes public distrust in AI to a broader crisis of trust in institutions.
He argues that people suspect tech companies of exploiting them, a distrust with deep historical roots.
Amodei rejects the idea of using positive marketing to rebuild trust, calling it deceptive.
He emphasizes that AI companies must deliver on their promises to benefit society to regain public confidence.
items.summary: Dario Amodei argues that public skepticism toward AI stems from a broader crisis of trust in companies, governments, and the tech industry. He contends that ordinary people suspect these entities of exploiting them, a distrust rooted in decades of history. Amodei dismisses the idea of using positive marketing campaigns to rebuild trust, stating that such efforts risk appearing deceptive. Instead, he emphasizes that AI companies, including Anthropic, must deliver on their promises to benefit society, which he views as the core issue requiring attention.
items.title: Amodei attributes public distrust in AI to broader trust crisis

key_points: Judges in Pakistan using JudgeGPT, an AI tool tailored to the country's legal system, resolved 6.3% more cases without a decline in judgment quality.
The tool, combining GPT-4 with a database of 128,292 Pakistani judicial opinions, was tested with 1,559 judges, with trained judges showing the most significant improvements.
Training was found to be crucial, with more trained judges using the tool persistently and resolving more cases per month.
While the study highlights efficiency gains, it acknowledges the need for judges to verify AI outputs and the unresolved question of whether justice quality has improved.
items.summary: A study in Pakistan found that judges using a custom AI tool called JudgeGPT, combined with training, resolved 6.3% more cases without a drop in judgment quality. The tool, developed by economist Sultan Mehmood and collaborators, integrates OpenAI's GPT-4 with a database of Pakistani legal texts. It was tested with 1,559 judges, with those receiving comprehensive training showing the most significant improvements. The tool helps with legal research and drafting, reducing time spent on case law searches and document summaries. However, the study acknowledges limitations, including the lack of direct human evaluation of judgment quality and the risk of over-reliance on AI. Researchers emphasize the importance of training to ensure proper use of the technology, while noting that efficiency gains may not fully address broader concerns about justice quality.
items.title: Pakistan's Judges Report 6.3% Productivity Boost with JudgeGPT AI Tool

key_points: Interconnects launched the Artifacts Hub to provide curated insights into open models.
The Adoption Dashboard tracks model downloads and usage by geography and organization.
The tools aim to enhance transparency and support the growth of the open model ecosystem.
The Artifacts Hub includes analysis of adoption metrics and intelligence from partners like Artificial Analysis.
The projects are part of Interconnects' mission to enable the open ecosystem through data sharing.

The Artifacts Hub provides curated insights into 792 models from the past two years, including adoption metrics and intelligence analysis. The Adoption Dashboard tracks model downloads and usage by geography and organization, highlighting the US-China adoption gap. These tools aim to support the open ecosystem by offering data-driven insights and fostering growth through shared analysis.
items.title: Interconnects Launches Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard to Track Open Model Ecosystem

key_points: AI labs are moving beyond model provision to higher stack layers to avoid the commodity trap.
Current AI business models face challenges due to undifferentiated models and low switching costs.
The authors suggest that AI labs must adopt enterprise software strategies to achieve durable profitability.
This shift risks customer lock-in and reduced competition, raising concerns about market concentration.
Historical examples show infrastructure providers rarely capture value, but cloud computing and chip fabrication have escaped the commodity trap through software-like properties or market dominance.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: Arvind Narayanan and Akash Kapur argue that AI companies are moving beyond model provision to higher stack layers to avoid the commodity trap. They highlight that current AI business models, reliant on inference charges, face challenges due to undifferentiated models, low switching costs, and price flexibility. The authors suggest that AI labs must adopt enterprise software strategies like vertical integration and switching cost creation to achieve durable profitability. They warn that this shift risks customer lock-in and reduced competition, raising broader concerns about market concentration and innovation. Drawing on historical examples, they note that infrastructure providers rarely capture value, but cloud computing and chip fabrication have escaped the commodity trap through software-like properties or market dominance. The authors caution that without regulatory intervention or structural changes, AI may follow a similar path to past infrastructure industries.
items.title: AI Labs Seek Profitability Through Stack Migration Amid Concerns Over Lock-In

key_points: AI has not replaced software engineers and is unlikely to do so, despite fears of job displacement.
The 'decide-execute-deliver' model shows AI automates the 'execute' phase but leaves decision-making and delivery resistant to automation.
Examples of AI-driven layoffs, such as at Block and Snap, often reflect financial pressures or restructuring rather than AI's direct impact.
Surveys show executives frequently cite AI as a reason for layoffs without evidence of actual implementation.
AI's productivity benefits are more evident in slower hiring rather than increased layoffs, with layoffs risking loss of organizational knowledge.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: The article argues that AI has not replaced software engineers and is unlikely to do so, despite widespread fears of job displacement. It examines the 'decide-execute-deliver' model of software development, noting that AI primarily automates the 'execute' phase but leaves the decision-making and delivery layers resistant to automation. The piece challenges narratives of AI-driven mass layoffs, citing examples like Block, Snap, and Intuit, where layoffs were often attributed to financial pressures or restructuring rather than AI. Surveys indicate that executives frequently cite AI as a reason for layoffs without evidence of actual implementation. The article also highlights that AI's productivity benefits are more evident in slower hiring rather than increased layoffs. While AI may reduce demand for certain roles, it does not eliminate the need for software engineers due to the complexity of decision-making and accountability. The authors conclude with cautious optimism, suggesting that the software engineering profession will continue to grow, albeit at a slower pace, as AI adoption progresses.
items.title: Software Engineering Jobs Remain Resilient Amid AI Adoption

key_points: Major oil companies are increasing their investments in nuclear fusion, signaling a shift from traditional energy sources.
Eni S.p.A. plans to deploy a commercial fusion power plant in Europe by the early 2040s, supported by its $1 billion agreement with Commonwealth Fusion Systems.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in July, bringing its total funding to $4 billion, with plans for a 400-MW plant in Virginia.
Other oil giants like Equinor, Chevron, Shell, and Cenovus are also backing various fusion technologies, with some aiming to build commercial power plants by the mid-2030s.
Eni is developing a tritium fuel-cycle facility to support future fusion reactors, as tritium is essential but difficult to obtain.
items.summary: Major oil companies are increasing their investments in nuclear fusion, signaling a shift from traditional energy sources. Eni S.p.A. plans to deploy a commercial fusion power plant in Europe by the early 2040s, supported by its $1 billion agreement with Commonwealth Fusion Systems. The company is also developing fuel systems for fusion reactors, leveraging its experience in hydrocarbon processing. Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in July, bringing its total funding to $4 billion, with plans for a 400-MW plant in Virginia. Other oil giants like Equinor, Chevron, Shell, and Cenovus are also backing various fusion technologies, with some aiming to build commercial power plants by the mid-2030s. Eni is developing a tritium fuel-cycle facility to support future fusion reactors, as tritium is essential but difficult to obtain. The article notes that commercial reactors will need closed-loop systems to recycle tritium, a challenge that Eni is addressing through its joint venture with the UK Atomic Energy Authority.
items.title: Big Oil Companies Invest in Nuclear Fusion Development

key_points: BYD is preparing to launch the Great Seagull, a larger version of its Seagull electric hatchback, by the end of 2026.
The Great Seagull will have a longer wheelbase and a more powerful 95 kW electric motor compared to the current 55 kW motor.
It is expected to include BYD's new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, along with advanced safety features like a LiDAR sensor.
The current Seagull offers two battery options with ranges up to 405 km, and the Great Seagull is anticipated to have a slightly higher price than the current model.
items.summary: BYD is set to release a larger version of its Seagull electric hatchback, named the Great Seagull, by the end of 2026. key_points: Maine's regulators selected an 800-MW wind farm and a 1.2-GW transmission line to advance clean energy.
The projects aim to reduce oil reliance in New England and generate $400 million in net benefits for consumers.
Regional cooperation among six New England states is unprecedented, with Maine covering less than 11% of the transmission cost.
Challenges remain, including financing, permitting, and public opposition, with past projects facing delays and cost overruns.
The federal regulatory environment for wind energy remains uncertain due to policy changes under former President Trump.
items.summary: Maine's utility regulators have selected an 800-megawatt wind farm and a 1.2-gigawatt transmission line proposal, marking a significant step toward clean energy development. The projects, proposed by Clearway Energy and Avangrid, aim to supply power to New England and reduce oil reliance. The wind farm could lower oil use by 10% in winter, with expected $400 million in net benefits for consumers and over 2,500 construction jobs. The transmission line, shared among six New England states, represents unprecedented regional cooperation. While the projects face challenges including financing and public opposition, advocates see them as a model for future clean energy efforts. The federal environment for wind development remains uncertain due to policy changes under former President Trump.
items.title: Maine selects wind farm and transmission plan for clean energy expansion

items.summary: The U.S. is increasing its oil influence in Iraq, aiming to secure a strategic position as the country plans to boost production to 8-10 million barrels per day within six years. Iraq's vast oil reserves, geographic centrality, and role in the Shia Crescent make it a key asset for global powers. Russia and China previously held significant influence through infrastructure deals and control over key regions, but the U.S. has moved to counter this through sanctions and new oil field acquisitions. ConocoPhillips has acquired a 42% stake in BP's Kirkuk oil fields, targeting production of up to 450,000 barrels per day. Chevron is developing the West Qurna 2 field and the Nasiriyah oilfield, supported by projects like the Common Seawater Supply Project. key_points: Dreame, a Chinese robot vacuum company, has canceled its rocket-powered electric hypercar and all car-related ventures.
The project, which included a hypercar with solid rocket boosters, was criticized as impractical and overly ambitious.
Internal sources suggest the car initiative was more of a marketing and fundraising effort than a serious product development.
Dreame’s exit follows a pattern of failed electric car projects by non-traditional automotive companies.
The company laid off nearly 1,000 employees in its car division, signaling a complete withdrawal from the automotive industry.
items.summary: Dreame, a Chinese company known for robot vacuums, has canceled its plans for a rocket-powered electric hypercar and all other car-related initiatives. The company, which announced its entry into the luxury electric vehicle market last year, unveiled a hypercar at CES and even planned an SUV to compete with the Rolls Royce Cullinan. However, its ambitions were deemed impractical, with the rocket boosters requiring recharging and the project appearing more as a marketing and fundraising effort than a serious manufacturing endeavor. CarNewsChina reports that Dreame is exiting the car business, having laid off nearly 1,000 employees in the department. The decision follows a trend of high-profile electric car project cancellations by companies not traditionally in the automotive industry, including Apple’s Project Titan and Sony/Honda’s joint venture. Analysts suggest Dreame’s project was overly ambitious and lacked sufficient detail, leading to its premature cancellation.
items.title: Dreame Abandons Rocket-Powered Hypercar and Car Division

key_points: Residential solar adoption in South Korea may lead to rebound effects where households offset some energy savings by increasing consumption after moving to lower tariff tiers.
The rebound effect is most pronounced for households that transition between tariff tiers, with savings offset ranging from 11-22%.
Net metering amplifies the rebound effect, doubling the offset for high-consumption households moving to cheaper tiers.
The study recommends incorporating tier-transition and net-metering factors into policy evaluations to better account for energy and emissions savings.
items.summary: A study by researchers Jiyoung Eum and Gyeong-Seok Choi reveals that residential solar adoption in South Korea can trigger rebound effects under the country's tiered electricity tariffs. The research shows households that move to lower tariff tiers after installing solar panels offset 11-22% of expected energy savings. Net metering amplifies this rebound effect, with high-consumption households seeing their offset double. The findings suggest policymakers should account for tier transitions and net-metering in evaluating solar programs. The study highlights the need for adjusted policy frameworks to address these rebound effects in energy and emissions savings calculations.
items.title: South Korean residential solar adoption may lead to energy rebound effects under tiered tariffs

key_points: Sweden's decommissioned solar panels could reach 150,000 metric tons by 2060, according to a new circular-economy roadmap.
RISE Research Institutes of Sweden estimates decommissioning volumes could range from 40,000 MT to 150,000 MT by 2060, depending on solar deployment and repowering rates.
The roadmap emphasizes the need for dedicated recycling infrastructure requiring an annual inflow of 10,000 metric tons to be economically viable.
Current panel waste is often mixed with general e-waste, limiting reuse opportunities and specialized recycling.
The report outlines five priority areas, including circular design, safer handling, and improved material recovery, to create a more circular solar industry.
items.summary: A new circular-economy roadmap by Axfoundation, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, and industry partners predicts Sweden's decommissioned solar panels could rise from 17 MT in 2021 to 150,000 MT by 2060. RISE Research Institutes of Sweden estimates this growth depends on solar deployment speed and repowering rates, with scenarios ranging from 40,000 MT to 150,000 MT by 2060. The roadmap highlights the need for circular solutions, including dedicated recycling infrastructure requiring 10,000 MT annual inflow. It warns that current panel waste is often mixed with general e-waste, limiting reuse opportunities. The report outlines five priority areas, including circular design, safer handling, and improved material recovery. It also notes that only six of 12 European countries met the 85% recovery target in 2021, under the EU's WEEE Directive.
items.title: Sweden's solar panel waste could reach 150,000 metric tons by 2060

items.summary: BCC Research predicts the global solar energy market will nearly double to $974.7 billion by 2031, growing at a 10.8% CAGR. key_points: Australia's grid-scale battery storage fleet has grown fourfold in three years, altering financing, contracting, and operational strategies.
Industry experts report a shift from physical tolls to commoditised battery storage contracts, with greater market interoperability.
Buyer profiles are diversifying, with 70% of parties in some projects not previously energy users, indicating a more sophisticated market.
Investor return expectations are rising, with 13-14% now demanded instead of 8-10%, driven by factors like rising debt costs.
Household battery storage systems, while growing rapidly, pose operational visibility challenges for grid planning and are unlikely to replace utility-scale services directly.
items.summary: Australia's grid-scale battery storage fleet has expanded fourfold in three years, reshaping financing, contracting, and operations. Industry experts at the Battery Asset Management Summit 2026 noted that spot prices and spreads are compressing, pushing operators to diversify revenue streams. Thomas Dargue of Eku Energy described a shift from physical tolls to commoditised products, with contracts becoming more interchangeable. Sally Torgoman of Ascera Energy highlighted a change in buyer profiles, with 70% of parties in her Riverina project not previously energy users. She emphasized the durability of system strength contracts over ancillary services. Investors now demand higher returns, with 13-14% expected instead of 8-10%. Jeremy Lloyd of Neoen noted declining ancillary services values as more capacity enters the market. Jake Dunstan of Aurora Energy Research pointed to delayed coal retirements as a disruptive factor. Household battery storage systems, while growing rapidly, pose operational visibility challenges for grid planning, though they are unlikely to replace utility-scale services directly. Torgoman cautioned against suppressing price signals, arguing that coal retirements will eventually drive market changes regardless of policy interventions.
items.title: Australia's battery storage market shifts toward commoditised contracts and diversified revenue streams

key_points: Five U.S. states are leading the adoption of energy storage to enhance grid reliability.
California has surpassed its 2024 storage target and now has over 21,000 MW of capacity.
Nevada reached its 2030 storage goal early, with bipartisan support across administrations.
Illinois aims for 3,000 MW of storage by 2030, with projected savings of $13.4 billion.
Virginia and Massachusetts are expanding storage capacity to meet rising electricity demand and affordability goals.
items.summary: Energy storage is becoming critical for maintaining grid reliability as electricity demand rises. Five states—California, Nevada, Illinois, Virginia, and Massachusetts—are leading the way in adopting energy storage policies. California surpassed its 2024 target of 1,825 MW, now with over 21,000 MW of capacity. Nevada, with bipartisan support, reached 1,700 MW by 2023, exceeding its 2030 goal. Illinois aims for 3,000 MW by 2030, with projected savings of $13.4 billion. Virginia, driven by data center growth, targets 16,780 MW of short-duration storage by 2040. Massachusetts has surpassed its 2025 goal and is expanding long-duration storage. These states demonstrate how energy storage can enhance grid reliability, reduce costs, and meet growing demand.
items.title: Five U.S. States Lead in Energy Storage for Grid Reliability

key_points: The NLR-NRRI alliance, called IMPACT, aims to demonstrate industry-scale technologies for critical minerals and materials.
IMPACT bridges research and commercialization by advancing technology readiness levels through collaborative facilities and expertise.
The partnership focuses on processes for metal recycling and recovery of critical minerals like lithium and copper, addressing challenges in scrap metal recycling and tramp element removal.
NLR’s Jennifer King leads the effort, emphasizing the alliance’s potential to scale innovations from concept to commercial application.
items.summary: The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) and the University of Minnesota’s Natural Resources Research Institute (NRRI) have launched the Joint Research Alliance for Innovative Materials and Processing for Advanced Critical Technologies (IMPACT). This initiative aims to demonstrate industry-scale technologies for critical minerals and materials, supporting U.S. manufacturing and supply chain resilience. IMPACT bridges research and commercialization by advancing technology readiness levels through collaborative facilities and expertise. The partnership focuses on processes for metal recycling and recovery of critical minerals like lithium and copper, addressing challenges in scrap metal recycling and tramp element removal. NLR’s Jennifer King leads the effort, emphasizing the alliance’s potential to scale innovations from concept to commercial application.
items.title: NLR-NRRI Alliance Demonstrates Critical Minerals Processing at Scale

It provides connectivity for drone pilots and field crews inspecting infrastructure in challenging environments.

items.summary: Windlab and Squadron Energy, a 50:50 joint venture, have submitted the Bungaban Solar Project for federal assessment under Australia’s EPBC Act. NYISO, the state's grid operator, faces challenges from 14 GW of pending grid connections, including 12 GW from data centers. The moratorium aims to provide time for regulatory planning, but its long-term effectiveness remains uncertain. key_points: Nuclear power plants face reduced efficiency and output during heatwaves due to high river temperatures or low water levels, impacting countries like France, Romania, and Hungary.
Gas power plants experience efficiency losses and capacity reductions as temperatures rise, affecting their ability to meet peak demand during heatwaves.
Wind generation is negatively impacted by reduced wind speeds during heatwaves, particularly in regions like Europe and Australia, though some areas may see increased wind.
The article critiques the tendency to blame intermittent sources like wind and solar for energy shortages during heatwaves, while underplaying the role of nuclear and gas plants.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: Heatwaves significantly affect various power generation sources, with nuclear, gas, and wind each facing distinct challenges. Nuclear plants, which rely on river water for cooling, often reduce output during extreme heat due to elevated water temperatures or low river levels, as seen in France, Romania, and Hungary. Gas power plants also experience efficiency losses and capacity reductions as temperatures rise, impacting their ability to meet demand. Wind generation is affected by reduced wind speeds during heatwaves, particularly in regions like Europe and Australia, though some areas may see increased wind. The article highlights that while heatwaves pose challenges, their overall annual impact on nuclear generation is minimal, and adaptation strategies are being developed to mitigate these effects. The piece also critiques the tendency to blame intermittent sources like wind and solar for energy shortages during heatwaves, while underplaying the role of nuclear and gas plants.
items.title: Heatwaves impact nuclear, gas, and wind power generation differently

key_points: HYDAC's Square Wave heat exchanger reduces clogging and improves cooling efficiency in wind turbine gearboxes.
Field trials showed turbines with Square Wave exchangers operated 20-25% cooler than conventional systems.
Improved thermal management supports better oil viscosity and reduced maintenance for aging wind fleets.
The technology offers a retrofit solution for enhancing turbine reliability without major system redesigns.
items.summary: HYDAC's new Square Wave heat exchanger design addresses cooling inefficiencies in wind turbine gearboxes, reducing clogging and improving thermal management. Traditional panel cut designs are prone to debris accumulation, leading to increased maintenance and reduced reliability. Field trials on GE and Mitsubishi turbines showed the Square Wave exchanger maintains cooler operating temperatures, with some turbines running 20-25% cooler than conventional systems. This improvement supports better oil viscosity, reduced maintenance, and increased turbine availability. HYDAC's Erickson notes that effective cooling is critical for long-term gearbox health and operational efficiency. The technology offers a retrofit solution for aging wind fleets, enhancing reliability without major system overhauls.
items.title: HYDAC's Square Wave Heat Exchanger Improves Wind Turbine Cooling Efficiency

key_points: The Bulgarian government has granted a targeted sanctions exemption to the Kozloduy NPP to allow imports from Russian suppliers.
The exemption aims to ensure nuclear safety and operational reliability by securing critical components and technical assistance.
The decision is limited in duration and applies only to specific contracts listed in the annexes.
Technical issues with non-Russian replacement parts led to shutdowns and economic losses at the Kozloduy plant.
The plant generates 30-40% of Bulgaria’s electricity and relies on Russian-origin systems for its operations.
items.summary: The Bulgarian government has granted a targeted sanctions exemption to the Kozloduy NPP, allowing imports of critical iron and steel products, original components, and technical assistance from Russian suppliers. This decision, under EU Council Regulation 833/2014, aims to ensure nuclear safety and operational reliability. The exemption is limited in duration and applies only to specific contracts listed in the decision’s annexes. The Kozloduy plant, which generates 30-40% of Bulgaria’s electricity, faced technical issues with non-Russian replacement parts, leading to shutdowns and economic losses. The plant’s Soviet-designed VVER-1000 reactors rely on Russian-origin systems, making alternative sourcing challenging.
items.title: Bulgarian government allows Russian imports for Kozloduy nuclear plant

key_points: EDF and Centrica are close to finalizing a £800m deal to extend Sizewell B's operation to 2055.
The extension aims to mitigate a projected nuclear generation gap as older reactors retire.
A Contract for Difference framework is being negotiated to stabilize power prices at £70 per MWh.
Centrica is expected to contribute £160m, reflecting its 20% ownership stake in the plant.
The extension supports energy security amid delays in new nuclear projects like Hinkley Point C.
items.summary: EDF and Centrica are nearing a £800m deal to extend Sizewell B's operating life to 2055, according to an EDF spokesperson. The agreement aims to address a projected nuclear generation gap as older reactors retire. Sizewell B, the UK's only pressurised-water reactor, provides 1.2 GWe, or about 3% of the country's electricity. The companies are negotiating a Contract for Difference framework with a proposed power price of £70 per MWh. EDF, owning 80% of the plant, and Centrica, with 20%, will split the costs, with Centrica contributing £160m. The extension supports power availability as new facilities like Hinkley Point C and Sizewell C face delays. Financial analysts at Citi view the £70/MWh strike price as attractive for returns. Centrica's interim results on 23 July will provide further clarity.
items.title: EDF and Centrica seek 20-year extension for Sizewell B nuclear plant

key_points: Economists developed a model integrating global firms and capital markets.

Financial and trade liberalization concentrate activity among large firms.
Welfare gains are larger in emerging and mid-sized open economies.
Market frictions amplify each other, reducing gains from liberalization.
items.summary: Economists Karabarbounis, Pellegrino, and Salomao developed a general-equilibrium model integrating global firms and capital markets. Using firm and country data, they analyzed how financial and trade liberalization concentrate activity among large firms, boosting welfare more in emerging and mid-sized open economies. They found product- and capital-market frictions amplify each other, reducing gains from liberalizing one market.
items.title: Global Firms and Capital Markets Model Evaluates Reallocation and Welfare Effects of Globalization

key_points: The study introduces a marginal cumulative multiplier to assess the impact of government spending and taxation on output during fiscal consolidations.
Researchers estimate a marginal spending multiplier of 1.5 and a marginal tax multiplier near 0 in their benchmark analysis.
Using the policy counterfactual method, they find spending multipliers consistently above 1.3 and tax multipliers below -1.
The findings contrast with existing literature, which often reports higher tax multipliers, suggesting scaling issues in previous studies.
items.summary: A new study by Roberto Perotti and Luca Sala examines marginal tax and spending multipliers during fiscal consolidations in 16 countries from 1978 to 2020. The research introduces a marginal cumulative multiplier to measure the effect of government spending or taxation on output while holding the other fiscal instrument constant. The authors estimate a marginal spending multiplier of 1.5 and a marginal tax multiplier close to 0 in their benchmark analysis. Using the policy counterfactual method, they find spending multipliers never below 1.3 and tax multipliers no higher than -1. The study suggests existing literature's higher tax multipliers may result from improper scaling of fiscal variables.
items.title: Study finds spending multipliers higher than tax multipliers in fiscal consolidations

items.summary: Adam Mosseri, head of Instagram, testified in a child safety trial against Meta, acknowledging that a 2021 feature to help teens manage screen time had low uptake. The feature, called Take a Break, was used by only 1.8% of teens, according to an internal document. Mosseri admitted Meta did not disclose this low usage rate to parents or users. The states suing Meta argue the company withheld information about the feature's ineffectiveness, violating consumer protection laws. Mosseri defended Meta's efforts to address teen overuse, noting multiple features were introduced. The trial is part of a broader legal challenge against tech companies over social media's impact on youth mental health. Potential penalties could reach $1.4 trillion, drawing comparisons to past tobacco litigation.
items.title: Meta's Adam Mosseri testifies about teen safety features and data transparency

The piece outlines the evolution of CD rates over the past two decades, noting that they fell to record lows during the 2000s and 2010s due to Fed policies and economic conditions. Owaisi also contrasted the stance of Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar with Muslim freedom fighters like Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi. He emphasized the role of Muslim figures in India's independence struggle, noting Maulvi Alauddin as the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands. The debate over Manusmriti intensified amid political clashes between BJP and Congress, with Rahul Gandhi criticizing the text's patriarchal views.
items.title: Owaisi criticizes RSS and BJP over Manusmriti opposition to Ambedkar's Constitution

key_points: Analysts suggest the Hindustan Copper OFS may not be attractive to retail investors despite a 10% discount.
The stock fell 7.04% to ₹533.20, with the OFS floor set at ₹514 per share.
Siddarth Bhamre warns that the discount alone does not justify investment due to limited upside potential.
Retail bids will open on Wednesday after the non-retail portion was oversubscribed.
Gaikar cautions that any copper price decline could erase the small price gap, advising against chasing short-term gains.
items.summary: Analysts warn that the Hindustan Copper OFS may not attract retail investors despite a 10% discount. The stock fell 7.04% to ₹533.20, with the OFS floor set at ₹514. Siddarth Bhamre notes the discount is not enough to justify investment, as valuations may not offer significant upside. Retail bids will open on Wednesday after the non-retail portion was oversubscribed. Gaikar highlights limited upside and risks of copper price declines, advising against chasing short-term gains.
items.title: Analysts caution retail investors on Hindustan Copper OFS due to limited upside

key_points: Mid- and small-cap stocks have outperformed blue-chip stocks, with the average advance-to-decline ratio reaching its highest level in four months.
Retail investors' preference for mid- and small-cap stocks has driven 56% of equity flows in August, compared to 40% in July.
The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 have gained 22% and 31% since April, outperforming the Nifty 50's 15% rise.
Analysts suggest broader market participation and value opportunities in smaller stocks explain the divergence in performance.
Large-cap funds experienced their first outflow in 30 months, signaling reduced appetite for blue-chip stocks.
items.summary: Mid- and small-cap stocks have outperformed blue-chip stocks, with the average advance-to-decline ratio reaching its highest level in four months. This indicates broader market participation, as retail investors favor these segments. In August, mid- and small-cap schemes received 56% of equity flows, compared to 40% in July, while large-cap funds saw outflows. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 have risen 22% and 31% since April, outperforming the Nifty 50's 15% gain. Analysts attribute this to strong earnings growth and value opportunities in smaller stocks.
items.title: Mid- and small-cap stocks outperform blue-chips as market breadth expands

key_points: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposes a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden.
Mamdani questions whether the city has legal authority to cancel the private gathering.
The event is part of the RSS's centenary-year global outreach programme and is expected to draw 5,000 participants.
Mamdani criticizes the RSS's exclusionary vision, aligning with his family's values of pluralism and secularism.
Interfaith groups have organized protests against the event, which the AHEAD Forum promotes as a message of global unity.
items.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposes a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden, stating the city may lack legal authority to cancel the private gathering. The event, part of the RSS's centenary outreach, is expected to draw 5,000 Indian diaspora members. Mamdani criticized the RSS's exclusionary vision, aligning with his family's values of pluralism and secularism. Protests against the event have been organized by interfaith groups. The AHEAD Forum promotes the event as a message of global unity.
items.title: New York Mayor Opposes RSS Leader's Event, Questions Legal Authority

key_points: Global brands have faced backlash for culturally insensitive campaigns, impacting their sales and reputations.
Target's Halloween costume was criticized for resembling a racist caricature, leading to its removal.
Starbucks faced a sales decline in South Korea over a campaign referencing the Gwangju Uprising.
American Eagle's ad campaign drew racial criticism, though the company claimed it expanded its customer base.
Anheuser-Busch InBev's Bud Light saw a sales drop after a social media promotion with a transgender influencer.
items.summary: Global brands have faced backlash for culturally insensitive campaigns, impacting their sales and reputations. Target's Halloween costume was criticized for resembling a racist caricature, leading to its removal. Starbucks faced a sales decline in South Korea over a campaign referencing the Gwangju Uprising. American Eagle's ad campaign drew racial criticism, though the company claimed it expanded its customer base. Anheuser-Busch InBev's Bud Light saw a sales drop after a social media promotion with a transgender influencer. Balenciaga and Gucci faced backlash for designs evoking blackface imagery. H&M and Pepsi faced criticism for ads perceived as racist, while Unilever's Dove and Zara also encountered controversies over their marketing choices.
items.title: Global brands face backlash over culturally insensitive campaigns

key_points: The government has expanded the Hindustan Copper OFS stake sale to 6% by exercising the full greenshoe option following strong non-retail subscription.
Retail investors can bid between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm on BSE and NSE, with at least 10% of the OFS size reserved for them.
The floor price of ₹514 per share may not reflect the actual price retail investors face due to institutional demand.
Analyst Vaqarjaved Khan warns the discount could disappear if institutional investors clear the OFS at higher prices.
While the company's Q1 profit surged 163% year-on-year, improved margins are attributed to higher copper prices rather than operational improvements.
items.summary: The government has exercised the full greenshoe option in the Hindustan Copper Offer for Sale (OFS), increasing the stake sale from 3% to 6%. This follows strong subscription of 3.41 times by non-retail investors on the first day of bidding. The OFS, open to retail investors on Wednesday, allows bids between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm on BSE and NSE. At least 10% of the OFS size is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares set aside for employees. The floor price of ₹514 per share, a discount to recent market prices, may not reflect the actual price retail investors face due to institutional demand. Analyst Vaqarjaved Khan notes the discount could disappear if institutional investors clear the OFS at higher prices. While the company's Q1 profit surged 163% year-on-year, improved margins are attributed to higher copper prices rather than operational improvements. Khan advises investors to consider the OFS for long-term copper exposure rather than short-term gains.
items.title: Government Exercises Greenshoe Option in Hindustan Copper OFS, Expanding Stake Sale to 6%

key_points: FIIDS warns that proposed $103,265 H1-B visa fees could push high-value jobs overseas.
Khanderao Kand said the fee could burden startups and companies with hundreds of millions in extra costs.
Combined with a potential $100,000 OPT fee, the policy risks making the student-to-work pathway unaffordable.
FIIDS cited a 17 per cent drop in international student enrolment and projected losses of up to $3.4 billion due to reduced international student numbers.
items.summary: The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) warns that proposed $103,265 additional H1-B visa fees could make hiring economically impractical, potentially shifting high-value jobs overseas. Khanderao Kand, FIIDS' Chief of Policy and Strategy, said the fee could burden startups and companies with hundreds of millions in extra costs. Combined with a potential $100,000 OPT fee, the policy risks making the student-to-work pathway unaffordable. FIIDS also cited a 17 per cent drop in international student enrolment and projected losses of up to $3.4 billion due to reduced international student numbers.
items.title: FIIDS warns H1-B fee hike may push high-value jobs overseas

key_points: Civil society groups in Bengaluru plan a September 1 campaign to highlight flaws in the SIR process.
Activists argue that high ADDSO numbers indicate improper conduct, with some genuine voters being incorrectly removed.
Jagruta Karnataka called for more time to file objections, while BJP spokesperson S Prakash defended the process, citing voter non-compliance.
items.summary: Civil society organisations in Bengaluru, including Eddelu Karnataka and Muslim Muttahida Mahaz, plan a September 1 campaign to highlight alleged flaws in the SIR process. Actor Prakash Raj endorsed the 'Election Commission Chalo' initiative, which aims to flag issues with the electoral roll data. Activists argue that high numbers under the ADDSO category suggest improper conduct, with some genuine voters being incorrectly removed. Jagruta Karnataka called for more time to file objections, while BJP spokesperson S Prakash defended the process, citing voter non-compliance.
items.title: Civil society groups plan September 1 campaign to highlight SIR flaws

key_points: Five family members were found dead in a lodge room in Srisailam, suspected to have committed a suicide pact due to financial difficulties.
The family overstayed their rented room, which was not permitted, and claimed to be unwell to avoid vacating.
Lodge staff noticed a foul smell before alerting police, who registered a case of suspicious death.
Temple authorities criticized the lodge for violating accommodation rules, which limit stays to 48 hours for devotees.
items.summary: Five family members were discovered dead in a lodge room in Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh, with police suspecting a suicide pact linked to financial struggles. The deceased included a 36-year-old man, his three sisters, and a 15-year-old nephew. Authorities noted the family had overstayed their rented room, which was not permitted, and had reportedly claimed to be unwell. The lodge staff noticed a foul smell before alerting police, who registered a case of suspicious death. Temple authorities criticized the lodge for violating accommodation rules, which limit stays to 48 hours for devotees.
items.title: 5 of family found dead in Srisailam; suicide suspected

key_points: The US has paused all visa applications and appointments globally as part of an immigration crackdown.
The initiative aims to limit access to applicants who may rely on state assistance, as stated by an official.
The State Department launched a global training program for embassies, with visa appointments to be rescheduled.
Applicants received emails informing them of cancellations and were promised new dates later.
items.summary: The United States has paused all visa applications and appointments worldwide as part of an immigration crackdown, according to the Financial Times. The move aims to limit access to those who may rely on state assistance, as stated by an official. The State Department announced a global training program for embassies, with visa appointments to be rescheduled. Applicants received emails informing them of cancellations and were promised new dates later.
items.title: US halts global visa appointments amid immigration crackdown

items.summary: Rajasthan Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Dr. Kirori Lal Meena was admitted to the ICU at Jaipur SMS Hospital after testing positive for swine flu. Meanwhile, protests erupted at IIT Delhi following the suicide of a physics student, with students demanding financial compensation, resignations, and an independent inquiry. In another case, a family in Andhra Pradesh died by suicide after alleging harassment and forced conversion by a rifle shooting coach. Additionally, an Indian loitering munition accidentally struck a sensitive Pakistani nuclear site during Operation Sindoor, raising concerns about military infrastructure vulnerabilities.
items.title: Rajasthan Minister Admits to Swine Flu ICU, Campus Protests Over Student Suicide

key_points: The Indian men's hockey team's World Cup performance has sparked alarm due to defensive lapses and poor decision-making.
Critics highlight the team's inability to convert pressure into goals and a weak midfield.
Former coach Jagbir Singh criticized the team's lack of consistency and questioned coaching strategies.
The team has less than three weeks to prepare for the Asian Games and the LA Olympics.
items.summary: The Indian men's hockey team's underwhelming performance at the World Cup has raised concerns, with critics pointing to defensive lapses, poor decision-making, and an ineffective attack. Despite moments of promise, the team conceded 16 goals in five matches, scoring 14, including five field goals. Former player and coach Jagbir Singh criticized the team's lack of consistency and questioned the coaching staff's strategies, particularly the midfield's inability to adapt. With less than three weeks until the Asian Games, the team faces pressure to improve ahead of the LA Olympics.
items.title: India's hockey team struggles in World Cup, faces criticism for poor performance

key_points: The US has paused visa appointments globally as part of a new training program for consular officers.
The State Department said the training will adjust visa schedules, though details remain unspecified.
The initiative aims to ensure comprehensive and consistent evaluation of visa applicants.
The move follows broader immigration crackdowns, including visa and green-card revocations.
The administration also plans to increase H-1B visa fees and tighten screening for applicants.
items.summary: The US has paused visa appointments worldwide as the Trump administration initiates a global training program for consular officers. The State Department said the training will adjust visa schedules, though details remain unclear. The initiative aims to ensure thorough screening of applicants for potential reliance on public benefits. This follows broader immigration crackdowns, including visa and green-card revocations, and legal challenges to some policies. The administration also plans to increase H-1B visa fees and tighten screening for applicants, while considering revoking business and tourism visas for those seeking asylum.
items.title: US halts global visa appointments amid Trump administration training push

key_points: SpaceX plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana, its largest launch site.
The project, named Starbase Louisiana, will feature over a dozen launch towers for more than 30 Starship flights per day.
The site will include facilities for propellant production, power generation, and deep-water shipping.
Construction is set to begin in 2027, with the first Starship launch expected in 2029.
The project is expected to create over 3,000 jobs and boost Louisiana's economy.
items.summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana, which will be its largest launch site. The project, named Starbase Louisiana, will feature over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day. The site, spanning 125,000 acres in Vermilion Parish, will include facilities for propellant production, power generation, and deep-water shipping. Construction is set to begin in 2027, with the first Starship launch expected in 2029. The project is expected to create over 3,000 jobs. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the investment, highlighting its potential for new jobs and economic growth. SpaceX aims to significantly increase rocket launches, including deploying space-based data centres by the end of next year.
items.title: SpaceX to develop $100 billion Louisiana spaceport with over a dozen launch towers

key_points: Anil Khandelwal resigned from Rashi Peripherals over governance concerns related to professional engagements with firms linked to two independent directors.
Khandelwal alleged that director appointments and management compensation were handled by company management, not the board's nomination committee.
The company's chairperson denied governance lapses, stating the engagements were at arm's length and within legal limits.
Rashi Peripherals' stock fell 10% following the resignation, with the company's market cap at ₹5,200 crore.
The resignation marks the second such instance this year, following a similar exit by Atanu Chakraborty from HDFC Bank.
items.summary: An independent director, Anil Khandelwal, resigned from Rashi Peripherals Ltd, citing governance concerns related to the company's professional engagements with firms linked to two of its independent directors. Khandelwal alleged that director appointments and management compensation were handled by company management rather than the board's nomination committee, and that due diligence for an acquisition was conducted by firms associated with the directors. The company's chairperson, Krishna Kumar Choudary, denied any governance lapses, stating the engagements were at arm's length and within legal limits. Rashi Peripherals' stock fell 10% following the resignation, with the company's market cap at ₹5,200 crore. The resignation marks the second such instance this year, following a similar exit by Atanu Chakraborty from HDFC Bank.
items.title: Independent director resigns over governance concerns at Rashi Peripherals

key_points: Demis Hassabis prioritizes scientific understanding over commercial metrics in AI development.
DeepMind's approach using deep reinforcement learning led to breakthroughs in games and protein folding.
The book highlights the competitive dynamics between DeepMind, OpenAI, and Chinese AI labs.
It raises ethical concerns about the unchecked development of powerful AI technologies.
Hassabis's career reflects a blend of personal ambition and a quest to unlock the mysteries of intelligence.
items.summary: Sir Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and founder of DeepMind, emphasizes his scientific approach to AI, aiming to understand nature and the universe. His work at DeepMind focused on AI applications in medicine and agriculture rather than chasing user metrics. The book 'The Infinity Machine' explores his career, from his origins in North London to his role in developing breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Hassabis's philosophy of deep reinforcement learning contrasts with early symbolic AI, allowing machines to learn through observation. The book also examines DeepMind's competitive landscape, including its response to OpenAI and the rise of Chinese AI labs like DeepSeek. It raises questions about the ethical implications of AI development and the challenges of managing its rapid growth.
items.title: Demis Hassabis's journey in AI and science

key_points: NITI Aayog's report highlights a structural imbalance in India's higher education system with millions pursuing generic degrees lacking job relevance.
Only 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications, and 13% of all graduates are unemployed.
The report calls for reimagining higher education through industry participation and PPP models to align curricula with industry needs.
It suggests moving toward specialised, job-linked programmes and expanding work-integrated learning to improve employability.
items.summary: NITI Aayog's report flags a structural imbalance in India's higher education system, where millions of students pursue generic degrees with weak job links. Only 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications, and 13% of all graduates are unemployed. The report notes that 1.86 crore students apply for just 55,000 government jobs, highlighting the mismatch between education and employment. It calls for reimagining higher education through industry participation and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to align curricula with industry needs. The report suggests moving toward specialised, job-linked programmes and expanding work-integrated learning to improve employability.
items.title: NITI Aayog highlights job mismatch in India's higher education system

key_points: Tamil Nadu's CM C Joseph Vijay scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, reversing a previous DMK government decision.
Protests from local communities and environmental concerns led to the project's cancellation, with Vijay citing displacement and farmland impact.
Current airport capacity is not yet at its limit, but experts warn of the long time required to develop a new airport and the risk of losing investment to other hubs.
Industry bodies urge the TVK government to expedite the search for an alternative site to avoid delays in infrastructure development.
The Parandur project was intended as long-term infrastructure, but the urgency of finding a new site remains due to the time needed for construction and clearances.
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, sending the project back to the drawing board. The decision, which the DMK's MK Stalin called an 'irreversible setback,' was made after protests from local communities concerned about displacement and environmental impact. While the existing Chennai International Airport has not yet reached its capacity threshold, experts warn that the long lead time for developing a new airport could delay necessary infrastructure. The airport's current capacity is expected to rise to 55 million passengers by 2026 with planned expansions, but industry bodies stress the urgency of finding an alternative site to avoid losing investment and talent to other regional hubs. The Parandur project, which would have handled 100 million passengers annually, was seen as long-term infrastructure rather than an immediate solution to congestion.
items.title: Chennai's Second Airport Project Back to Site Selection After Parandur Scrapped

key_points: Crude oil prices dropped 6% over two days, with Brent crude at $86 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $80.42.
Market reactions are driven by developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran-Oman talks.
JPMorgan estimates prolonged disruption could push Brent prices up by $7-$8 per barrel.
Goldman Sachs warns of potential $120 per barrel if disruptions continue, but forecasts Brent to average $80 in Q4 and $75 next year.
items.summary: Crude oil prices fell 6% over two days, with Brent crude at $86 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $80.42, reacting to developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran-Oman negotiations. JPMorgan estimates prolonged disruption could push Brent prices up by $7-$8 per barrel, while Goldman Sachs warns of potential $120 per barrel if disruptions continue. However, the bank forecasts Brent to average $80 in Q4 and $75 next year, with risks tilted to the upside due to ongoing tensions.
items.title: Oil prices drop 6% amid Strait of Hormuz tensions and Iran-Oman talks

key_points: Banks in several Indian states and Union Territories will close on August 26 for Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi.
The Reserve Bank of India classifies August 26 as a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act.
Physical branches in cities like Mumbai and Delhi will be closed, while others in Ahmedabad and Jaipur will remain open.
Online banking and UPI services will continue to function during the holiday.
Upcoming bank holidays include August 28 for religious observances and August 30 for a weekly holiday.
items.summary: Banks in multiple Indian states and Union Territories will close on August 26 due to Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi. The Reserve Bank of India lists this day as a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Branches in cities like Mumbai, Delhi, and Chennai will remain shut, while others in areas like Ahmedabad and Jaipur will operate normally. Online banking and UPI services will remain functional. The next major holidays are August 28 and August 30.
items.title: Banks in several states close on Eid-e-Milad, August 26

key_points: Hindustan Copper has opened its OFS for retail investors with a 10% discount on the floor price of Rs 514.
The government plans to sell a 3% equity stake as part of the base offer, with an additional 3% available as a green shoe option.
The OFS, valued at nearly Rs 2,982 crore, received strong demand from non-retail investors, leading to the exercise of the greenshoe option.
A minimum of 10% of the offer size is reserved for retail investors.
Analysts note that the discount is already stale, and the stock has sharply crashed more than 7% on the opening day.
items.summary: Hindustan Copper has opened its offer for retail investors, with a 10% discount on the floor price of Rs 514. The government plans to sell a 3% equity stake as part of the base offer, with an additional 3% available as a green shoe option. The OFS, valued at nearly Rs 2,982 crore, received strong demand from non-retail investors, leading to the exercise of the greenshoe option. A minimum of 10% of the offer size is reserved for retail investors. Analysts note that the discount is already stale, and the stock has sharply crashed more than 7% on the opening day. The government's divestment efforts continue with this OFS, following recent stake sales in other PSUs.
items.title: Hindustan Copper OFS opens for retail investors with 10% discount
