Gandhi's speech criticized Modi's stance on women protesters and referenced patriarchal norms from the Manusmriti.
The debate highlights the tension between acknowledging political progress and maintaining feminist integrity.
Critics argue that focusing on Gandhi's credentials risks ignoring broader political consequences, such as the BJP's Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act.
The article questions whether feminists should prioritize ideological purity or strategic engagement in a system where power is unevenly distributed.
items.summary: Feminists are divided over Rahul Gandhi's call to 'smash the patriarchy,' with some arguing that his political intervention deserves recognition despite his imperfections, while others demand ideological purity. Gandhi's speech at the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme in Pune criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's stance on women protesters and referenced the Manusmriti's patriarchal norms. The debate highlights the tension between acknowledging political progress and maintaining feminist integrity. Critics argue that focusing on Gandhi's credentials risks ignoring the broader political consequences, such as the BJP's Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, which marginalizes trans people. The article questions whether feminists should prioritize ideological purity or strategic engagement in a system where power is unevenly distributed.
items.title: Feminists Debate Rahul Gandhi's Patriarchy Criticism Amid Political Realities

key_points: GIVA's Rakshabandhan ad featuring Kriti Sanon sparked a social media debate over cultural norms and women's clothing choices.
Critics argued the outfit was inappropriate for the festival, while supporters defended it as a reflection of evolving social norms.
Public figures like Kangana Ranaut and Rahul Gandhi commented on the controversy, with Ranaut questioning the attire and Gandhi supporting Sanon's right to personal expression.
Sanon responded by emphasizing that the essence of festivals lies in emotions and traditions, not clothing, and criticized ongoing scrutiny of women's attire.
GIVA withdrew the advertisement and issued an apology, stating it had no intention of offending cultural sentiments.
items.summary: GIVA's Rakshabandhan advertisement featuring Kriti Sanon ignited controversy over cultural traditions and women's clothing choices. The ad showed Sanon wearing an Indo-Western outfit and tying a Rakhi to both her onscreen brother and a pet dog, drawing criticism from social media users who deemed the outfit inappropriate for the festival. BJP MP Kangana Ranaut and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also weighed in, with Ranaut questioning the choice of attire and Gandhi defending Sanon's right to personal expression. Sanon herself emphasized that the essence of festivals lies in emotions and traditions, not clothing. In response to the backlash, GIVA withdrew the advertisement and issued an apology, stating it had no intention of hurting sentiments related to Indian culture and traditions.
items.title: GIVA's Rakshabandhan ad sparks debate over cultural norms and women's clothing choices

key_points: Gurugram's real estate boom has led to the loss of 75% of stormwater drains and a third of ponds, causing severe flooding during heavy rains.
The city ranks among the world's worst for air pollution and has poor groundwater quality, with many residential areas relying on generators.
Urban development in Gurugram has prioritized construction over planning, resulting in deforestation, wetland encroachment, and inadequate drainage systems.
Land prices have skyrocketed, creating a corrupt nexus between developers, politicians, and bureaucrats, with real estate money funding electoral politics.
Experts argue that the real estate boom has consumed land that once absorbed rainwater, leading to recurring floods and structural vulnerabilities in the city's infrastructure.
items.summary: Gurugram, India's 'millennium city', faces severe flooding and environmental degradation due to its real estate boom. Nearly 75% of stormwater drains and a third of ponds have been lost to construction, leaving the city vulnerable to waterlogging during heavy rains. The city also ranks among the world's worst for air pollution and has poor groundwater quality. Urban development has prioritized construction over planning, with forests cleared and wetlands encroached upon. Land prices have skyrocketed, creating a corrupt nexus between developers, politicians, and bureaucrats. Critics argue that the real estate boom has consumed land that once absorbed rainwater, leading to recurring floods. A state survey and geo-tagging data show extensive loss of natural drainage systems, while experts blame institutionalized corruption for the city's structural vulnerabilities.
items.title: Gurugram's real estate boom leads to severe flooding and environmental decline

key_points: IMF chief says the global economy has weathered the oil shock better than feared due to AI investment and increased non-Gulf supply.
Georgieva highlights a tug-of-war between the West Asia energy shock and AI-driven demand growth, with uneven impacts across countries.
Risks include rising bond yields, stalled disinflation, and potential financial instability from AI, with low-income countries most vulnerable.
The IMF lowered its 2026 growth forecast to 3% and will revise it again in October.
items.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva stated that the global economy has weathered the oil shock from the Strait of Hormuz closure better than feared, thanks to factors like AI investment and non-Gulf supply increases. She noted a tug-of-war between the negative supply shock from West Asia and the positive demand shock from AI, with impacts varying by country. Georgieva warned of risks including rising bond yields, stalled disinflation, and potential financial instability from AI. She emphasized that low-income countries face greater challenges due to energy dependency and AI adoption gaps.
items.title: IMF chief highlights global economy's struggle between oil shock and AI growth

key_points: Welspun Corp shares dropped 6% following a block deal where the CEO and promoter group sold a stake worth Rs 1,433 crore.
The transaction was executed at Rs 2,275.30 per share, a 3% discount to the previous closing price.
The sale involved 63 lakh shares, representing 2.4% of the company's outstanding shares.
The deal was secondary, meaning the company did not receive any proceeds from the sale.
Promoter and management stake sales are closely watched by the market for their potential impact on sentiment.
items.summary: Welspun Corp shares fell 6% after the CEO and promoter group sold a stake valued at Rs 1,433 crore through a block deal. The transaction, executed at Rs 2,275.30 per share—a 3% discount to the previous closing price—involved the sale of 63 lakh shares. The deal, which was secondary, did not generate proceeds for the company. Welspun Investments and Commercials, along with CEO Vipul Mathur, were the sellers. The stake represented 2.4% of the company's outstanding shares. The market closely monitors promoter and management stake sales as they can influence investor sentiment.
items.title: Welspun Corp shares drop 6% after CEO, promoter group likely sell stake worth Rs 1,433 crore via block deal

key_points: Cyient targets double-digit revenue growth and 15% EBIT margins by FY28-29.
The company is shifting from project-based to annuity-based contracts, with 40% of revenue currently from project-based work.
Motilal Oswal maintains a Sell rating with a 24% downside, citing back-ended recovery and flat FY27 organic growth expectations.
Nuvama raises its target price to Rs 1,050, highlighting expanded total addressable market to $2.4-3.2 trillion.
PL Capital adjusts EBIT margin estimates to 13.5% and 14.0% for FY27 and FY28, maintaining a Hold rating with a 6.5% upside.
items.summary: Cyient aims to achieve double-digit revenue growth and 15% EBIT margins by FY28-29, shifting from project-based to annuity-based contracts. The company reported a record $300 million in large-deal pipeline and described FY26 as a stabilization year. Motilal Oswal maintains a Sell rating with a 24% downside, while Nuvama raises its target price to Rs 1,050, citing expanded TAM to $2.4-3.2 trillion. PL Capital retains a Hold rating with a 6.5% upside, adjusting EBIT margin estimates. Cyient also introduced CYINGINE to support AI adoption.
items.title: Cyient outlines growth strategy with EBIT targets and expanded market opportunities
